summary: Radar for 2026-11-03, GLP-1 focus. This snapshot brought little new randomized data. Today's PubMed and news feeds mostly refresh topics we already track. The main new item: on 2 Nov 2026 at the AHA Scientific Sessions, researchers presented an observational, not yet peer-reviewed study of 256,492 adults with prediabetes and obesity. Compared with metformin, GLP-1 medicines were linked to a 31% lower risk of developing type 2 diabetes. It has early news pickup (AHA newsroom, Medical Xpress, AJMC). It suits a carefully hedged Short, not a long-form. Two other news hooks: Medscape's 2 Nov piece "GLP-1 therapies not linked to fracture risk in three studies" (a bones body-worry Short; one real-world cohort did flag tirzepatide, so it must stay balanced), and a 3 Nov Cureus case report of liver injury after an unregulated product sold as "retatrutide". The case report adds to Victoria's June 2026 alert (6 cases) and this week's Malaysian seizures, so it fits a "what's confirmed?" retatrutide Short as the week's single gray-market Short. Checks on other new-looking items: the FDA approval of Mounjaro for heart risk (scanx, 1 Nov) happened on 28 Aug 2026, and the US approval for children with type 2 diabetes was in Feb 2026, so neither is new. I found no fresh randomized head-to-head against tirzepatide or semaglutide in the last 48 hours, so no extra long-form (L2) is triggered. The Lane A long-form queue from the playbook still ranks highest (hair loss, stopping, fatigue, birth control, injection site, dehydration), with fresh review-level refreshes. Thanksgiving content should ship before the 18–27 Nov peak. ObesityWeek (14–17 Nov) and the rest of AHA week are the next data windows. Rejected: online and compounded tirzepatide programs, sellers of "research" retatrutide peptides, and coverage and cost stories.

candidates.topic: Tirzepatide hair loss: will it grow back? A verified long-form redo. 5.4% (119/2,183) vs 0.9% (22/2,221) (Gupta 2026); the label reports 7.1% of women vs 0.5% of men. Refreshed by the Med Sci (Basel) systematic review of skin side effects (9 Oct 2026) and the Cureus semaglutide cutaneous RCT meta-analysis (30 Sep 2026)
candidates.angle: Answer first: hair shedding on tirzepatide is usually linked to rapid weight loss, and the shedding type known as telogen effluvium tends to be temporary. Then a 'you' scenario: noticing more hair in the brush at month 4. Cover what the label counts, why women report it more, and what supports regrowth (protein, steady intake). End with when to see a doctor or dermatologist. Use the craft-note figures and wording word for word. It's the only path from the 1,019-view Short to a long-form.

candidates.topic: What happens when you stop tirzepatide? SURMOUNT-4: 783 began the lead-in, then 335 vs 335 were randomized at week 36. Those switched to placebo regained 14.0% from week 36 to week 88. Refreshed by the 12-month real-world tirzepatide study (Diabetes Obes Metab, 28 Oct 2026)
candidates.angle: Answer first: in SURMOUNT-4, people switched to placebo regained part of their lost weight, while people who stayed on tirzepatide kept losing. Then the honest 'you' framing: obesity behaves like a long-term condition. Cover habits that help (protein, strength training) and the questions to bring to your prescriber. Include 'don't switch, stop or change your medicines on your own'.

candidates.topic: Will tirzepatide weaken my bones? Medscape (2 Nov 2026): 'GLP-1 therapies not linked to fracture risk in three studies'. The evidence is mixed: one real-world cohort linked tirzepatide to higher osteoporosis or fragility-fracture risk than other GLP-1 medicines (HR 1.44); others found neutral or lower risk
candidates.angle: An 08:00 body-worry reassurance Short with a balanced answer: most studies so far don't show more fractures with GLP-1 medicines, but one cohort flagged tirzepatide. All of these are observational ('linked to'). Weight loss itself can lower bone density, which is why protein and strength training matter. Ask your doctor about bone health if you have risk factors. Funnel to the live Bones & Muscle long-form.

candidates.topic: Retatrutide: what's confirmed vs the 'research peptide' products. Cureus case report (3 Nov 2026) of liver injury after an unregulated injectable sold as retatrutide; Victoria health alert (6 liver-toxicity cases, June 2026); Malaysian Health Ministry seizures of illegal retatrutide (2 Nov 2026)
candidates.angle: A 13:00 'what's confirmed?' Short with a loop ending. Confirmed: retatrutide is still in trials and isn't approved anywhere. The Phase 3 results so far are trial data (TRANSCEND-T2D-2 topline, 28 Oct). Products sold online aren't the trial drug, and health authorities have linked some of them to liver injury. Calm tone, no scare framing, and send people to their prescriber for approved options. Counts as the week's single gray-market Short.
